resources.string: Your Nextcloud photos in Android’s system photo picker
Not signed in. Sign in to your Nextcloud to see its photos in the photo picker.
Nextcloud refused this app’s password, so the library has stopped updating. Sign in again to resume.
Signed in as %1$s\n%2$s\nChoose the folders that hold your photos.
This deletes the app’s password on your server and removes the library and cached photos from this phone. The picker’s Nextcloud tab stays empty until you sign in again.
Signed out on this phone. The server couldn’t be reached, so remove the app password in Nextcloud under Settings, Security.
Enter your server’s address. You approve access on your server’s own sign-in page, and this app gets its own app password, which you can revoke in Nextcloud under Settings, Security.
Approve access on the sign-in page, then come back to this app.
This address uses plain HTTP, so your password and photos cross your network unencrypted. Use https:// if your server supports it.
That doesn’t look like a server address.
Plain HTTP is allowed only for servers on your local network. Use an https:// address.
Couldn’t find this server. Check the address and your connection.
Couldn’t connect to the server. Check the address and your connection.
The server’s certificate isn’t trusted. If it uses your own certificate authority, install that certificate in Android’s security settings.
No Nextcloud found at this address.
This Nextcloud isn’t fully installed yet.
The server is in maintenance mode. Try again later.
The server returned an error. Try again later.
The sign-in page expired. Continue to start again.
No browser is available to open the sign-in page.
Your server is on your local network. Android blocks apps from reaching local devices unless you allow it, so the next screen asks for that permission.
Without local network access, Android blocks this app from reaching your server.
Changing folders rebuilds the library. The picker’s Nextcloud tab empties and fills again as the new folders are listed.
Your server refused NC Media Provider’s app password, so your photos have stopped updating. Tap to sign in again.
Your Nextcloud server asked to wipe this device, so the account, its library and its cached photos were removed from this phone.
Updating the app deselected it in the photo picker. Tap to open the picker’s cloud settings and select it again.
Not listed yet. The first sync starts as soon as the network allows.
Sync queued. It starts when the network allows.
Couldn’t reach the server. Trying again soon.
Local network access not allowed. A server on your home network can’t be reached without it.
Allow full photo and video access so files already on this phone are handed over directly instead of being downloaded again.
Full photo and video access granted
Full access not granted. Copies from your server still work over the network.
Android only lets allow-listed apps act as a cloud photo source, and only one can be selected at a time. The status below checks both.
This app is allowed and selected as the picker’s cloud source.
This app is allowed. Select it in the photo picker’s cloud settings.
This app is not on Android’s cloud provider allow-list yet.
Photo picker settings aren’t available. If you just activated this app, restart the phone once and try again.
Optional: Shizuku can apply the same settings as the ADB commands below, without root.
Shizuku is not running. Open its manager to install or start it.
This Shizuku version is too old. Version 11 or newer is required.
Shizuku is running. Grant this app access to continue.
Shizuku access was denied. You can allow it from Shizuku’s app settings.
Shizuku did not start the activation service in time
Could not open Shizuku or its download page
This app is now allowed as a cloud source. Open the photo picker settings and select it.
This app is now the photo picker’s cloud source. Open the picker in any app to see your Nextcloud photos.
The settings are saved, but this phone turns on the picker’s cloud sources only at startup. Restart the phone, then tap Activate with Shizuku again to select this app.
Keep Google Photos as a choice
Enable Developer options and USB or wireless debugging, then run these commands once. The last one selects this app; if it prints false, restart the phone and run it again.
These commands put Android’s settings back the way they were:

Only one cloud source can be active at a time. With Google Photos kept as a choice, you switch between it and this app in the photo picker’s cloud settings. On some phones, such as GrapheneOS, that settings screen only appears after a restart. Updating this app deselects it; with Shizuku it is selected again automatically, otherwise a notification takes you to the settings.
The system photo picker is unavailable
The library, the last sync and the downloaded media. Old downloads are removed automatically at the limits shown.
